title: Short-Baseline Neutrino Anomalies: From LSND to SBND and Everything in Between
desc: Abstract: Short-baseline neutrino anomalies have held the community’s attention for more than two decades, with the persistent 4.8σ MiniBooNE excess standing as a tantalizing hint of physics beyond the Standard Model. Recent MicroBooNE results have substantially redrawn this picture: comprehensive searches strongly disfavour the traditional light sterile neutrino explanation, yet the anomalies themselves remain unexplained. That tension has driven an exciting shift toward richer theoretical frameworks. Dark-sector models with new mediators, enhanced couplings, and novel production mechanisms now provide compelling alternatives that speak both to the anomalies and to broader questions of neutrino mass generation and dark matter. I will review the MicroBooNE experimental results, discuss…

We discuss questions related to representation and parameterization in global ocean climate modelling. title: Nature-inspired computation: real world challenges and opportunities
desc:
Continued advances in Frontier AI capabilities were achieved through escalating compute, electricity, cooling, water and infrastructure demand.

Further progress, and the full realisation of the potential societal benefit of this technology, is now constrained not only by computational model quality, but by the physical limitations, energetic and environmental costs of the underlying computational infrastructure.

In light of a clear need for cheap, low energy, sustainable compute solutions, researchers and innovators have been exploring different physical signals that could potentially transform future computing paradigms.
